He died of Covid after being sick for only six days and my mom couldn't function, so Amber (I'm almost positive that's her name) helped me walk her through all the paperwork, which was so easy to finish, if you had your wits about you. Show less Read more Like 1.8K Dislike Reply 31 replies Hide replies 31 replies @jeanabeana8818 6 years ago My Mom was cremated 10-years ago this April 7. It was what she wanted, but hearing how it happened made me feel at ease...she died of a very aggressive cancer and to know it burned up, setting her soul free, just gives me a sense of calm and joy. She's free of pain and suffering and the diseased body she left behind is gone forever. I miss her dearly, but I know I'll see her again one day. Show less Read more Like 19 Dislike Reply @TukikoTroy 6 years ago Thank you for including temperatures in Celsius... You know, for the rest of the world. Show less Read more Like 2.7K Dislike Reply 123 replies Hide replies 123 replies @Spongebobs4Life 8 years ago (edited) My cousin’s grandma died last summer, and she requested a wicker coffin. However, she was on the, erm, larger side, and when they got the wicker coffin (which was essentially a long basket-a nice one mind you) it wasn’t strong enough for her to be carried into the church by the pall bearers, as the bottom was making a, well, worrying noise. We were assured that it would hold, as it had a wooden plank on the bottom, but obviously her son wasn’t wanting to take the chance of his dead mother falling through the bottom of her coffin on the way to be buried, so the church provided a little trolly, like an aeroplane, hostess trolly, that they covered with a black curtain, and placed the coffin on top to wheel her around. It was oddly dignified, and quite lovely, until my youngest cousin (age 13) loudly exclaimed, “this was a wheely good idea!”. There’s a place for mediocre puns, and apparently a funeral is not the place. Rest well, Anne. The engraving will say our names and, "No coffee for us today, we are sleeping in." We both love/d coffee. *Edit: I love coffee, he loved coffee and has already passed on from a motor vehicle accident. Show less Read more Like 476 Dislike Reply 6 replies Hide replies 6 replies @dramac333 4 years ago (edited) Thank you so very much! When my wife passed away in April of 2020, I followed her instructions and had her body cremated. She wanted no services, no memorials, no obituaries. Her one request was that I find "a really pretty jar for her to live in." All of that was exactly what I gave her, and all of that is also what I have instructed our daughter to do with my body. After that, she can do whatever she wishes with both sets of remains. She seems to think that she will do the same thing to her daughter that we're doing to ours, but her daughter says (and this is an exact quote): "Ha! Fat chance! Dumpster City here I come!" And that is perfectly fine with me. I don't plan to be there. But since my wife was cremated, I have always wondered about the process, so thank you for this post!
